newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria aims to guarantee future profits.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria aims to guarantee future profits.

text.p: Spanish banking group Corporacion Bancaria de Espana (Argentaria) said on Friday that it has made strategic changes to guarantee recurrent income in the future.
In a statement accompanying its 1996 results, Argentaria said management had adhered to "principles of transparency, quality and recurrent results.
"Solid bases have been set up on which to guarantee the future generation of recurrent results in forthcoming years and in such a way so that these offer an ever-increasing contribution to profits."
Argentaria said that its ability to generate recurrent earnings had risen because of a strong fall in institutional financing costs.
The bank has reduced items of marginal profitability on both the loan and institutional side, prioritising growth on retail banking.
In 1996, the group formed Gesinar to centralise all the foreclosed assets of the group in order to significantly reduce their balance and realise any latent value in those assets.
Argentaria last year also significantly increased its stakes as a financial investor in Telefonica de Espana, the final state stake of which is currently being privatised, and utility Endesa.
"These are investments that offer important synergies in light of the future development of the group's banking business," the statement said.
